introduction: This level shifts to the actual vessels where reactions take place. Examiners heavily target the design equations of the three ideal reactors (Batch, CSTR, and PFR) and test you on graphical volume comparisons using Levenspiel plots.

core_concepts.title: Batch Reactor
core_concepts.description:
An unsteady-state, closed system. Reactants are charged initially, the reaction proceeds over time, and products are discharged at the end. 
Design Equation: **$t = N_{A0} \int_{0}^{X_A} \frac{dX_A}{-r_A V}$** 
(For constant-density liquid systems, $V$ remains constant).

core_concepts.title: CSTR (Continuous Stirred Tank Reactor)
core_concepts.description:
Also known as a Mixed Flow Reactor (MFR). Operates at steady state. It assumes perfect, instantaneous mixing. Consequently, the concentration everywhere inside the reactor is perfectly equal to the exit stream concentration.
Design Equation (Algebraic): **$\tau = \frac{V}{v_0} = \frac{C_{A0} X_A}{-r_A}$**

core_concepts.title: PFR (Plug Flow Reactor)
core_concepts.description:
A tubular reactor operating at steady state. It assumes absolutely zero radial mixing and no axial dispersion. The concentration of reactants drops gradually along the length of the tube.
Design Equation (Integral): **$\tau = \frac{V}{v_0} = C_{A0} \int_{0}^{X_A} \frac{dX_A}{-r_A}$**

important_entities.name: Space Time ($\tau$)
important_entities.significance:
The time required to process one complete reactor volume of fluid based on entrance conditions. 
Formula: $\tau = \frac{V}{v_0}$ (Where $v_0$ is the volumetric flow rate). 
**Space Velocity:** The exact inverse of space time ($1/\tau$).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation:
The Biggest Exam Trap: For a given conversion and flow rate, which reactor requires a larger volume? 
Because a CSTR always operates at the lowest possible concentration (the exit concentration), its reaction rate is the lowest. 
- For $n > 0$ (Positive order): **$V_{CSTR} > V_{PFR}$**.
- For $n < 0$ (Negative order): **$V_{PFR} > V_{CSTR}$**.
- For $n = 0$ (Zero order): **$V_{CSTR} = V_{PFR}$**.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: CSTR is a Box, PFR is the Curve
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: On a Levenspiel plot ($1/-r_A$ vs. $X_A$), the volume of a CSTR is the area of a large rectangle, whereas the volume of a PFR is the exact area under the curve. This visually proves why CSTR volume is larger for normal kinetics.

exam_strategy_tips: A favorite GATE and PSU numerical concept: 'For a first-order reaction requiring 90% conversion, which ideal continuous reactor will have a strictly smaller physical volume?' Answer: PFR.
